name: tt-vo-3
text: India's Supreme Court ordered these two towers blown up. Taller than Qutub Minar, and nobody ever lived in them. So why destroy them? It starts with a garden. In 2009, the builder's new plan put two towers on green space promised to residents. Then they grew. Twenty-four floors became forty. The problem? They stood nine metres from an existing building. The rules asked for sixteen. And nobody asked the residents. So the residents went to court. In 2014, the High Court said, demolish. In 2021, the Supreme Court agreed, and said Noida's planning authority had colluded. Buyers got refunds with twelve percent interest. Then, in August 2022, 3,700 kilos of explosives. A ten-year fight, over in seconds. Was it the right call... or a waste?
